source.title: Beyond Parameters: Exploring Virtual Logic Depth for Scaling Laws
source.authors: Rui-Ke Zhu; Han-Wen Zhang; Kevin Y. Li; Tian-Yu Shi; Yi-Qun Duan; Chi Wang; Tian-Yi Zhou; Arindam Banerjee; Zeng-Yi Qin

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. Some figure results are described qualitatively but their numerical values are not stated in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies parameter reuse and virtual logical depth (VLD), measuring reasoning accuracy and knowledge capacity. It does not test or rely on the held-out cross-entropy power laws, their extrapolation, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. as background, but reports no held-out pretraining-loss sweep, loss-law fit, large-run extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation experiment. Its results on reasoning accuracy and random-sequence knowledge capacity are related scaling findings, but measure different outcomes; they are recorded with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. only as background. It reports no held-out pretraining cross-entropy, no loss-law fit, no extrapolation, and no compute-optimal allocation. Its measures are synthetic iGSM reasoning accuracy, post-SFT benchmark scores, and memorised entropy on random token sequences. The VLD experiments change effective depth at fixed parameter count, which is close to V4's question, but they measure reasoning accuracy and memorisation capacity rather than held-out loss. So no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that VLD substantially improves reasoning while keeping knowledge capacity nearly constant, whereas classical scaling raises knowledge capacity with parameter count (they say linearly). They report that smaller VLD models can beat larger standard models: a 50M cycle ×2 model reaches 62.05% vs 61.15% for a native 150M model. They note occasional non-monotonic results.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates tied-layer reuse and reasoning/knowledge-capacity measures rather than fitting held-out cross-entropy scaling laws or finding compute-optimal parameter/token splits.
record.method_sensitivity: Reasoning accuracy varies with VLD pattern, repetition factor, and which layers are reused; the paper reports occasional non-monotonic results.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed parameter count, tied-layer reuse (VLD) raises synthetic iGSM accuracy, depending on pattern and factor. Example: 4-layer cycle ×5 reaches 70.7% vs 46.3% base. Inverse-cycle ×1 lowers accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Effective depth via parameter reuse can improve reasoning accuracy without adding parameters; the effect depends on reuse pattern, factor and layer placement.

fits_no_version.finding: Memorised information on random sequences rises with parameter count (5M–20M) but stays nearly flat under VLD at fixed parameters. Shown only in a figure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Knowledge (memorisation) capacity tracks parameter count, not effective depth.

fits_no_version.finding: After LoRA SFT, the Cycle-VLD variant of LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct beats Base on Math500, GPQA, AIME, HumanEval and MBPP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer reuse added before fine-tuning can raise downstream benchmark scores.

record.peer_reviewed: Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2026; arXiv.org preprint
record.problems: The study does not report held-out cross-entropy results relevant to the claim. Table 1 reports means over 2–3 checkpoints without error bars, and the authors say multi-seed statistics remain future work. Figure 4's knowledge-capacity results are described qualitatively without numerical values in the text. The experiments cover a limited set of model sizes and configurations.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolating loss from small runs to much larger ones.
Loss at fixed parameter count across depth, width or shape. VLD varies effective depth but no loss is reported.
Power-law loss in other modalities or regimes. Fine-tuning results are benchmark accuracy, not loss laws.
Predictability of downstream performance from scale or loss. Native 4/8/12/16-layer iGSM accuracies are shown, but no fit or prediction is made.
Dependence of exponents or allocation on setup or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The title invokes 'scaling laws', but no power-law fit or loss measurement appears. Native-depth baselines (12-layer ≈150M at 61.15%; 16-layer only in Figure 3a) are not in the rows. They bear on no version, so they are not listed as missing. Table 1 values are means over 2–3 checkpoints with no seeds or error bars, so small differences (e.g. ±1–2 points) may be noise.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation as a function of compute.
Loss differences attributable to depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
Predictability of downstream performance from model scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices.
